subject: Integration bootcamp: SDK start guide & cutover checklist
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Integration bootcamp: SDK start guide & cutover checklist

Hi Kevin —

Thanks again for agreeing to the integration bootcamp next week. I put together a short starter bundle to help your engineers get a safe PoC running and plan the endpoint migration window. Attached: sdk-quickstart-v1.zip (includes language samples, env templates).

High-level asks for this thread:
- Confirm who will attend the 90-minute technical workshop on 2028-07-07 (we have one calendar slot on the Drive link below).
- Review the cutover checklist (we'll run a brief canary, then a staged traffic migration).
- Quick alignment on retries/timeouts and rate-limit behavior so we can provide sample configs.

Quick notes from our side:
- SDKs: official Node/Python/Go clients included. Default retry uses exp backoff, disabled for streaming endpoints.
- Endpoint migration: we recommend a 3-phase canary (1%, 25%, 100%) with 15-minute observation windows. Metric watch: 4xx/5xx rates, p95 latency, token cost per request.
- Rate limits: hosted accounts start at 600 rps with per-minute burst allowances; we'll provide per-route guidance for your workflows.

Attached: sdk-quickstart-v1.zip, a short retry-patterns.pdf and the canary-cutover-checklist.xlsx are in the Drive folder.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Integration-Bootcamp
Calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=integration-workshop-2028-07-07

If you can confirm attendees and preferred cutover weekend by EOD tomorrow, we'll finalize the workshop exercises.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
(attachment: sdk-quickstart-v1.zip)

From: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@fintegrate.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration bootcamp: SDK start guide & cutover checklist

Thanks, Irene — really helpful packet. A couple quick clarifications from our infra lead: 

1) Migration window: our ops team prefers a midnight-to-4am window (PST) for minimal user impact. Is that compatible with the staged approach you suggested?
2) Retries: what's the recommended behavior for idempotent vs non-idempotent calls? We plan to call generation endpoints with inline user content (non-idempotent).
3) Rate limits: can we request a temporary bump for the canary? Last time we saw token spikes on first writes.

Attendees: me and our infra lead, Priya Shah (cc'd in a follow-up).

I'll also export the SDK and run the Python quickstart today.

—Kevin
Kevin Liu
Head of Platform, Fintegrate

Kevin — thanks for the heads-up. For coordination: 

- Workshop: we booked 2028-07-07 09:00-10:30 PST. Please confirm Priya Shah or another infra attendee.
- Pre-work: run the Python quickstart and paste a sample request/response to the shared Drive folder. That helps Vivek instrument the right dashboards.
- Canary owner: please nominate an on-call engineer who can make the rollback call during the window. We will be on-call as well.

Attached is an editable canary-cutover-checklist.xlsx — fill in your cutover owner, AWS region, and expected peak TPS. We'll prepare the final runbook and a DocuSign for the temporary quota bump.

Marissa

Thanks — confirmed. Priya Shah (priya.shah@fintegrate.com) will join the workshop and act as our canary owner. We completed the Python quickstart; I uploaded a sample request/response to the Drive folder.

Quick clarifications before the workshop:
- We'll use the midnight-4am PST window on 2028-07-14 for the canary. Please confirm Redwood can provision the temporary rate bump starting 2028-07-14 00:00 PST through 2028-07-14 06:00 PST.
- We will implement server-side dedupe tokens for generate calls. Any examples or a lightweight middleware you can share ahead of the call would be great.
